title: The fare isn't the point. The silence is.
subtitle: An inclusive fare doesn't mainly save money. It removes a week of small transactions.

text: No single upsell is expensive. Thirty of them are exhausting.
sub: The drinks package, the cover charge, the spa tier, the internet plan. Each one reasonable on its own, and collectively a running negotiation with your own holiday.

points.label: Embarkation day
points.value: The drinks package, decided in a queue, before you have seen the bar.

points.label: Dinner, most nights
points.value: Which rooms carry a cover charge, and whether tonight is worth one.

points.label: Sea day, morning
points.value: The thermal suite tier. Day pass, three days, or the whole voyage.

points.label: Port day, four o'clock
points.value: The tour desk, and a queue of people making the same late decision.

points.label: Disembarkation eve
points.value: The folded statement, and the small shock of the total.

quote: An inclusive fare is a line deciding not to sell you anything else once you're aboard. Restraint is the product.

title: Three things that shift when nothing is sold

items.head: You order the second coffee
items.body: Small permissions compound. A week where nothing is metered is a week you actually use.

items.head: You try the room you'd have skipped
items.body: Cover charges quietly ration curiosity. Remove them and people wander, which is the point of a ship.

items.head: The crew stop selling
items.body: Where nobody carries an upsell target, the conversation at the bar becomes a conversation. That is the real change.

text: Cost both sailings to the same finish line, then read the friction.
sub: Sometimes the inclusive fare costs more and is still the better week. What you are buying is the absence of asking, and no brochure has ever managed to photograph that.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with
body: Or send me the two fares you're comparing and I'll cost them both to disembarkation morning — the number that actually decides it.
